memories.content: Do not exceed two primary HCI contributions.
Name each design or empirical contribution and present it in a single sentence.
In studies recruiting community participants, emphasize the time burden associated with participation.
In studies recruiting community participants, emphasize the travel burden associated with participation.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to identify primary contributions when named design or empirical contributions exceed two.
Emphasize the core design decisions that formative evaluation will change rather than a polished product demonstration.
Emphasize design principles transferable to other similar interactions as the primary contribution, rather than the performance of a specific prototype.
Formative evaluation creates grounds for modification in subsequent iterations rather than definitively determining the superiority of design alternatives.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess result reproducibility if the system version used in the field deployment is not disclosed.
Record changes in system configurations, field procedures, and data collection tools during deployment, along with their timestamps and rationales.
The history of deployment versions and configuration changes provides necessary evidence for interpreting results from different field sites.

analysis.overview: The reference frame guides contribution framing, community-participant burden, and formative evaluation. The compared frame independently addresses deployment provenance and change documentation for reproducibility and cross-site interpretation. The frames contain no materially shared or competing operational policy.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories jointly express a one-sided contribution-presentation policy and its reviewer-centered rationale; the compared frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Primary HCI contributions should be limited, explicitly named, and stated concisely so reviewers can identify them.

relations.reason: The two reference-side memories split the same one-sided burden-reporting claim into its time and travel dimensions; the compared frame does not address participant burden.
relations.summary: Community-participant studies should emphasize participation burdens involving both time and travel.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories jointly characterize the iterative purpose and appropriate presentation of formative evaluation, a subject absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation should foreground design decisions open to revision and support subsequent modification rather than claim polished or definitive superiority.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only claim about contribution emphasis, with no operational counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Transferable design principles, rather than a particular prototype's performance, should be presented as the primary contribution.

relations.reason: The compared-side memories form one deployment-documentation policy covering what provenance to preserve and why it matters; the reference frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Deployment provenance should disclose system versions and record timestamped configuration, procedure, and data-tool changes with rationales to support reproducibility and cross-site interpretation.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance calls for disclosing deployed system versions and timestamping configuration, procedure, and data-tool changes with rationales so field results remain reproducible and interpretable across sites.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance limits and clearly names primary contributions, highlights participant time and travel burdens, and frames formative work around transferable principles and iterative design change.
